claim: The tracer particles emit at 680 nm, as specified by the supplier for the product family.
validity_conditions: A single number where the physical object is a band: the sheet prints 'Emission: 680 nm' and gives no width, so the bandwidth is unstated rather than narrow, and a filter chosen as if 680 were the whole emission is a choice made on missing information. Diameter-independent, so this holds before the tracer_diameter_unknown gap closes. Entered separately from the excitation peak deliberately -- the two are one product specification but not one claim, and a caller picking a dichroic can be wrong about one while right about the other. mic-20260918-001:v2:widefield_inline:a6 asked for emission_wavelength at 18:45 today and got `absent`; that answer stands at its pin and this entry does not reach back to it. CONTRADICTED BY A MEASUREMENT ON THIS SETUP, 2026-09-19, AND NOT TO BE COMPUTED FROM. The person measured 605 nm here; this sheet says 680 nm. The measurement is a `calibration:` source at E2 and therefore OUTRANKS this entry -- 10.3 rule 1 says a run elsewhere is not a run here, and a vendor's characterisation is exactly that. This entry is not a misreading of the document: the sheet does print 680 nm, and what is disputed is whether the document describes the bottle on this bench. THE GAP IS NOT A DISCREPANCY, IT IS A DIFFERENT DYE. 680 nm is the Cy5 / Alexa-647 family and 605 nm is the Cy3 / TRITC family. These are not two estimates of one peak that differ by a few percent -- a dye emitting at 680 nm seen through a filter passing 605 nm returns almost nothing. So one of the two is wrong about this bottle, and the candidates are named: either the product identification is wrong, or the filter set named is not the one that will actually be used. The identification is the first suspect because of how it was made -- from a vendor listing, not by reading a label off the bottle. NOT YET ENTERED, AND DELIBERATELY SO. The measured value needs a cal_id, a measurement date and a `validity` saying what was measured under which conditions, and only the person can supply them. Entering it now would recreate the state this store was in on the morning of 2026-09-19, a `calibration:` asserting E2 with no validity period -- except that the schema now refuses it, which is precisely the moment a seat starts inventing a cal_id to get past the gate. Waiting is the correct action. Its `valid_until` will be an EVENT and not a date: the validity condition is the bead lot, because dye loading varies from lot to lot. WHETHER THIS IS EVEN ONE OBSERVABLE IS OPEN. A dye's emission peak and the band a filter set actually passes are two different facts, and A6's diffraction limit needs the second -- the wavelength that is actually imaged. Carrying both under one name would leave no way to tell from a card which one was used. Raised with both managers; until it is settled the corrected value has no name to be entered under, which is a second and independent reason it waits. MEANWHILE NOTHING MAY BE BUILT ON EITHER VALUE. A6's diffraction limit was about to be built on this entry and has been stopped; A1's abstention changes character too, from `no number for tracer_brightness` to `this combination may produce no signal at all`. THIS ENTRY IS NOT DELETED AND WILL NOT BE. Rule 7 keeps both sides and rule 8 deletes nothing. The reason is forward-looking: the next person to find this data sheet will propose 680 nm again, and what stops them is a record that it was examined and contradicted by a measurement. A published specification being wrong about the thing on the bench is itself worth knowing.
